comment:
The Ministry of Health of Slovenia welcomes this draft and considers it a substantial and useful piece of work. Our comments are offered from the position of a country that has operated a national clinical record since 2015 and is now extending it across several care settings through separately procured applications.

Our substantive comments concentrate on one structural matter, and we state that openly so the shape of this submission is clear. The guidance treats exchange, coded meaning and logical structure substantively, and each is given named standards or a named component. The persistence layer — the form in which a country's clinical data is held over a lifetime, and the standard that governs it — is not treated in the same way, and the places where the guidance does touch it are not consistent with one another. Because that layer determines what a country can do for decades afterwards, and because it is the layer our own experience bears on most directly, we have commented on each place where it arises. The remaining comments address conformance, cross-border flows, financing, workforce, the goal mappings, the country examples and a number of editorial matters.
